title: Grab and Move being too powerful part 2: lock screen can be moved

judgment.rationale: The report claims Grab and Move can reposition the Windows lock screen, but provides only a two-step reproduction and no current-version confirmation. Confirm before proposing a target-exclusion change; do not request credentials or any lock-screen secret.
evidence: Report uses 0.99.1 and says the issue occurs after locking and triggering Grab and Move.
Author suggests LockApp class/executable may be relevant.
Pinned Grab and Move resolves a top-level target and applies exclusions, but the snapshot does not establish the lock-screen target identity.
judgment.recommended_action: Confirm current reproduction and exact gesture without collecting sensitive lock-screen information.

fix_assessment.rationale: A current reproducer and actual target-window identity are not available; no specific exclusion is proposed until the lock-screen window is identified.

issue_context.summary: Grab and Move was reported to move the Windows lock screen.

No comments, logs, or linked fixes are present.
inferences: The target may be a lock-screen window not excluded by current eligibility logic, but this remains unverified.
issue_context.analysis: The safety boundary merits a focused current reproduction and target identity, not generic diagnostics.
initial_investigation: Read report and timeline; no comments or attached bug report.

information_gaps.information: Whether the lock screen can still be moved on the current release, plus the exact Grab and Move gesture and whether the machine is locked when the gesture starts.
information_gaps.why_needed: The issue claims the Windows lock screen moves when Grab and Move is triggered, a sensitive UI boundary. It has no bug report or comments, and source target filtering alone does not establish how the lock-screen window is classified.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On current release reproduce only if safe; report version, modifier/button gesture, and whether the lock screen changes position. Do not share credentials or unlock information.

comment.body: Thanks for reporting this lock-screen behavior. Could you confirm whether it still reproduces on the current release and state the exact configured modifier/button gesture? If so, please tell us whether the lock screen itself moves (without sharing any account, password, or unlock details). The report mentions LockApp.exe as a possibility, but we need to confirm the current target before proposing an exclusion.
